findings.description: `validChunk()` accepts zero-length payloads for every chunk of a nonempty file, and `done()` marks the transfer complete after receiving the expected indexes without checking the assembled file. When the original owner has left, a room participant can claim to hold an existing print, become the selected source, and send empty chunks that the recipient reports as a successfully received photo.
findings.title: Guests can save empty files as photos

findings.description: `isValidJoins()` rejects an entire layout if it references a departed device, but the leader retains that device’s joins in `s.joins`. After a joined device leaves, the leader keeps broadcasting the stale join alongside later valid joins, so guests reject every subsequent layout.
findings.title: Guests miss joins after a device leaves

findings.description: `keyReady` resolves after five seconds even without a key, and `relay()` then returns without sending its queued frame. If a valid peer key arrives later, the initial print announcement has already been discarded, and the newcomer has no automatic path to receive that print.
findings.title: Slow key exchange loses shared photos

findings.description: `onMessage()` allocates and retains `new Array(m.n)` for each previously unseen file ID without bounding the peer-supplied count or the number of transfers. A room participant can send incomplete chunks with many IDs or large counts, leaving those allocations and their retry work active indefinitely.
findings.title: Crafted chunks can exhaust device memory

findings.description: `onSignal()` resolves `keyReady` only after the received public key derives successfully, without recovering from malformed key input. An invalid first key signal leaves relay sends to that claimed peer waiting indefinitely, and the shared relay queue then blocks sends to other peers too.
findings.title: A bad key stalls encrypted delivery

findings.description: The `layout` broadcast handler assigns `payload.joins` on every non-leader without validating the sender or value. A participant can broadcast `{ joins: null }`, making those devices throw on every frame when `solveLayout()` iterates the value.
findings.title: A forged layout stalls guests' tables

findings.description: `visible()` rejects a print when its anchor is no longer in the current layout, even if another device still has the print. When the uploading device leaves, presence removes its screen from the layout and the remaining devices stop drawing its photos.
findings.title: Photos vanish when their screen leaves

findings.description: `onMessage()` stores a peer's `print` fields without checking their shape, and `frame()` calls `p.type.startsWith()` on the stored value. A room participant can omit `type` in a print message, causing every subsequent animation frame that draws it to throw.
findings.title: A crafted print freezes table drawing

findings.description: `onPush()` queues every room broadcast and resets its resolution timer without validating the claimed device or limiting batch size. A participant can continuously defer legitimate joins, or submit many compatible forged pushes to drive the leader's exhaustive pairing search into prolonged main-thread work.
findings.title: Forged orb pushes can stall joining

findings.description: The README tagline states that nobody in the middle can see shared photos, but the same README's Known gaps section admits the room server could swap public keys, which is an active man-in-the-middle position that reads every file. Users who rely on the tagline will trust the relay with content it can actually decrypt.
findings.title: README promises a private channel the app cannot deliver

findings.description: The Join form accepts any non-empty string up to 12 characters and `start()` uses it unchanged as the Realtime channel name `photo-<code>`, so a short hand-typed code such as TEST is guessable and anyone can enumerate the room. The comment on line 52 and the lobby hint promise a code people cannot guess, but that holds only when the New room button fills the field, and the page never warns that a typed code is weaker.
findings.title: Typed room codes can be guessed by anyone

findings.description: The newcomer catch-up loop announces only prints whose original owner is the current device. If that owner leaves but another device retains the print and its bytes, a later guest receives no metadata with which to display or request it.
findings.title: Late guests miss photos still held

findings.description: `onSignal()` processes ICE candidates concurrently with asynchronous remote-description setup and discards candidates when `addIceCandidate()` fails. If a candidate arrives before its offer or answer has finished applying, it is never replayed, so an otherwise viable direct link may fall back to the slower relay.
findings.title: Early connection candidates get lost

findings.description: The receiver creates `incoming` state only after a chunk arrives, while the retry timer examines only that state. If all initial chunks of a requested file or thumbnail are lost during a relay interruption, the sender receives no retry request and the transfer remains incomplete.
findings.title: Lost first chunks never get retried

findings.description: `thumbOf()` lets an image-decoding failure reject into the file pick handler, which does not catch it. If one selected image cannot be decoded for a thumbnail, it and every later file in that selection are skipped before being placed on the table.
findings.title: One unreadable image blocks the batch
